## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `448bac5da0780e8787cca5ee514dca17ff57482b`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, against: the card (objectui#11569 body, triage `5972410418`, claim `5977893924`, dev report `5978370413`, seat review `5978394943`); the PR body, its six-file list and the net diff `origin/main` `2e818d0`..`448bac5` (merge-base is `2e818d0`, one commit); the published `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0 tarball (`npm pack`, `dist/ui/index.mjs`); objectui `main` `2e818d0` and the head by `git show`. Check-runs on the head at the final read (2026-10-04T09:23:01Z): 43 runs, 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard)`, `dependabot`), 0 failed, 0 in progress; the head is still `448bac5`. The one PR comment is the performance-budget and bundle-size bot; no bot re-read a pending changeset, so no paragraph is judged false there. The seat's review was read as a claim to test, and every reading below is my own.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The page compile accepts a `dataSource`-bound `record:line_items` node with no `childObject`: right.** The diff removes `required: true` from that one input and adds a `description`; nothing else moves in `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx`. The spec row (17.6.0 `RecordLineItemsProps`) reads `childObject: z.string().optional()`, described "Optional because the component-level `dataSource` binding can supply the object instead". The runtime agrees: `ElementDataSourceGate` (`packages/react/src/element-data-source/ElementDataSourceGate.tsx`) writes `next[objectKey] = composed.object` whenever a binding is present, and `RECORD_LINE_ITEMS_DATA_SOURCE` maps `object` to `childObject`. The page compile was the only face refusing what the row, the zod faces and the renderer accept. Pinned by rows 2 and 3 of the new test, red first and ablated.

2. **The neither-node now compiles too: consistent with the row and the ruling, not a hidden authoring error.** The row's own describe continues "with neither, the panel shows a configuration hint and fetches nothing": the published contract already accepts the neither-node and names the runtime hint as its answer. Triage says the same ("The runtime's visible config hint for a node with neither stays the answer there") and forbids new manifest vocabulary in this card. The refusal the gate used to raise was one the contract never asked for; `objectui validate` accepted the neither-node before and after. The hint is visible and pinned (`LineItemsPanel.childObjectDecline.test.tsx`, unchanged and green; `form.lineItems.noChildObject` renders the property name as code). The trade-off is stated in the changeset body ("A node that names its child object in neither place also compiles now"). Whether a one-of form is wanted is a question for its own card; see ③ item 6.

3. **The "no one-of-required vocabulary" finding is true.** `ComponentInput` (`packages/types/src/base.ts`) carries `required?: boolean`; its zod twin `ComponentInputSchema` (`packages/types/src/zod/base.zod.ts`) carries `required: z.boolean().optional()`. `ManifestInput` (`packages/sdui-parser/src/types.ts`) carries `required?: boolean` and `binding?: 'object'`, the latter documented as "the input NAMES an object", not requiredness. `validateTree`'s only requiredness read is `if (input.required && !(input.name in node))` (`validate.ts`), and its only binding read records a site, waiving nothing. No either-or form exists on either type or in the compiler.

4. **No document that compiled before is refused now.** The diff removes one check and adds a `description`. `validateTree` reads `description` nowhere (its one occurrence is the base-prop table); the serializer forwards it as a passive field (`sdui-parser/src/index.ts`). Monotone widening. `relationshipField` and `columns` stay `required: true`, and row 4 of the pin is the before-and-after control on that.

5. **Emitted typings and block list: right, and nothing regenerated is owed.** `sdui.manifest.json`, `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` and `sdui-blocks.md` are written by `buildArtifacts` (`packages/sdui-parser/scripts/gen-manifest.ts`) at build time; none is tracked at `main` `2e818d0` (`git ls-tree`). `childObject?: string` and the required column `relationshipField, columns` follow from the same manifest entry; row 1 of the pin reads that entry from the shipped manifest.

6. **The published description is accurate.** "`dataSource.object` lands on this key, outranking an authored value": the gate's precedence table reads "`dataSource.*` keys are authoritative" and the compose is unconditional. "With neither, the panel shows a configuration hint naming this key and loads nothing": the panel declines both fetches on a falsy `childObject` and renders the hint with the property as code. The description opens with the row's own describe, as the calendar, gantt, map and timeline `objectName` inputs do.

7. **What publishes.** `@object-ui/plugin-form`'s `record:line_items` registration (the `ComponentRegistry` entry's `inputs`) loses `required: true` on `childObject` and gains a `description`; the host-emitted manifest entry, typings and block list move from it. No export of `@object-ui/plugin-form`, `@object-ui/types` or `@object-ui/sdui-parser` is added, removed or renamed; `packages/types` is untouched, honouring objectui#8347's hold.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes` is right.** The page compile is a public door and its accept set widens: a bound node, and the neither-node, go from `ok: false` to `ok: true` (the PR's own table). A published registration's declared input changes shape. That is the declaration's criterion, and the honest direction.
- **`patch` does not match it. The changeset must grade `@object-ui/plugin-form` `minor`.** The fleet rule is explicit: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch` UNLESS the PR declares `Clause-②: yes`, in which case at least `minor` (objectstack AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist item 3, recording the maintainer ruling "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface takes at least `minor`"); the fleet's `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` LEVEL axis mechanises it and names the pair in this PR by shape: "A declaration of ① plus a `patch` in ② is a self-contradiction inside one PR". objectui's own practice agrees where the declaration is `yes`: `.changeset/11564-flex-bag-children-list.md` on `main` reads "shipped as `minor` per this repository's version policy", and the closest precedent, `element:number`'s `object` no longer `required` because the binding supplies it (dd0d78f, PR objectui#10944, 2026-09-28, objectui#10909), declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and graded `@object-ui/components` `minor`, under Minor Changes in its CHANGELOG with the banner. The PR body cites that landing as the shape it repeats, then grades below it.
- The precedent picture, read in full so the seat can weigh it: the two older landings of this shape, PR objectui#10390 (3ef0b51, 2026-09-24, map and gantt) and PR objectui#10508 (875ee61, 2026-09-25, calendar), declared `Clause-②: no` and shipped `patch`, each a consistent pair; objectui#10944 declared `yes (widening)` and shipped `minor`, also consistent. This PR pairs `yes` with `patch`, which is neither. Flipping the declaration to `no` to keep `patch` is not open: the accept set measurably widens and the claim has declared it. objectui's `Changeset Bump Policy` check judges `major` only (its `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` has no LEVEL axis), so its green carries no information on this axis.
- The claim `5977893924` prescribed "one `@object-ui/plugin-form` `patch` changeset" beside `Clause-②: yes`, so the contradiction originates in the dispatch; the dev executed the claim as written. The repair is one line in `.changeset/11569-line-items-child-object-optional.md`, `patch` to `minor`; the body already describes the widening. Recommended, not required: open the body's second paragraph with the `**Clause-②: yes (widening)**` banner the repository's recent minors carry.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Pin in `apps/console`, not `plugin-form`: accepted.** It reads the manifest the console ships (`emitSduiManifest` over `dev/manifest-registry.ts`), the save gate's own input, through the same import pair `sdui-manifest-build-11403.test.ts` already uses in that directory; a `plugin-form` placement would add `@object-ui/sdui-parser` as a devDependency for one test. `@object-ui/console` is versioned, but the change there is a test file, so no second changeset is owed; `Changeset Declaration` is green.
2. **Comment-only rewrites and the `data-source.md` sentence: accepted, each sentence checked.** The two old comments said `childObject` was `required: true` on the registry entry (false after this diff) and that the block "has no spec schema at all" (false since 17.6.0's `RecordLineItemsProps`); the replacements state that the row and the entry both leave it optional and name the binding, which is what this review measured. The docs sentence's three clauses (a bound node needs no `childObject`; the page compile accepts it; the neither-node shows a hint naming `childObject` and loads nothing) each match the gate compose, the compile result and `form.lineItems.noChildObject`. Prose faces are outside the contract tier; judged here because the brief asked.
3. **Hypothesis 4 falsified: confirmed.** `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` at `2e818d0` has no read of an input's `required` (29 textual hits, all `requiredPermissions` members or prose); it reads `input.type` and `input.of`. Unchanged is right.
4. **Family finding: right to fold, right that it is outside this card.** At `2e818d0`, `object-grid` (`plugin-grid/src/index.tsx`), `object-kanban` (`plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx`) and the `plugin-dashboard` registrations still declare `{ name: 'objectName', type: 'string', required: true }` while their 17.6.0 rows make `objectName` optional for the binding. Triage scoped this card to one registration and forbade new vocabulary. The seat filed objectui#11605 (open, unlabelled, awaiting triage) as the family's closing card; nothing from it is owed here.
5. **`LineItemsPanelSchema.childObject` stays `string`: the acceptance note is the right carrier, with one correction to its framing.** The type IS a published export (`packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` line 67 re-exports it), not only an internal prop type. Leaving it is still right: it types the panel's input AFTER the gate composes the binding, where `childObject` is present on every bound node; the two fetch guards handle the `undefined` case; and loosening a published type is a second Clause-② surface outside this card. No defect, no card.
6. **Escalated to the seat, not blocking.** Whether a "one of these is required" manifest form is wanted at all is the question triage left open ("If one is wanted, it is its own card"). Nothing in this diff presumes an answer; with objectui#11605 lining up six more registrations that will drop `required` the same way, the seat may want the question in the decision box before the family closes rather than after.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-11569-line-items-childobject`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FjqrwXPfSMkSfkKYDSRkN2`

Written 2026-10-04T09:24Z. FAIL on ② alone, the changeset level. ① and ③ hold. A patch round that regrades `@object-ui/plugin-form` to `minor` on this diff, with the check-runs green on the new head, is the whole of what a PASS needs.
